title: fix(plugin-designer): read a lookup's target under the retired `referenceTo` spelling too (objectui#8058)
body:
Fixes #8058

## What was broken

`MetadataFieldsPage` had two halves that did not meet. The **read door** (`toDesignerField`) set `referenceTo: raw.reference` — the spec spelling and nothing else. The **write door**'s `carryOver` strips `referenceTo` from the carried-over server definition (the objectui#6527 tombstone site), and `fromDesignerField` re-emits the target as `reference`.

For a field whose target survives **only** as the pre-objectui#6041 `referenceTo`, the read found nothing, the strip removed the stored value, and the field reached the wire as a `lookup` with no target at all — saving silently at `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0, and answering `422 INVALID_METADATA` at `fields.NAME.reference` against 17.3.0 with nothing naming which field.

## The change

`storedRelationshipTarget(raw)` reads `reference` and falls back to `referenceTo`; `toDesignerField` uses it. That is all of the behaviour change.

## P1 — measured before writing a line, because the ruling hung on it

The dispatch made the fix conditional on `referenceTo` and `reference` carrying **the same value shape** across the objectui#6041 rename. Measured against the installed artifact (`pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `@objectstack/spec` to **17.4.0**):

```
FieldSchema.safeParse({ type: 'lookup', label: 'L', referenceTo: 'account' })
  => success = false
  => unrecognized_keys — "Did you mean `referenceTo` → `reference`?"
FieldSchema.safeParse({ type: 'lookup', label: 'L', reference: 'account' })
  => success = true
```

Three readings, all pointing the same way:

1. **The spec itself calls them one key under two spellings.** `referenceTo` is one of five entries `FieldSchema`'s alias map renames onto `reference` (`relatedTo`, `target`, `targetObject`, `lookupObject` are the rest), and `src/ui/view.zod.ts` says so in prose: *"`reference` is the key `FieldSchema` accepts — `referenceTo` is only a rejected alias it lists so a failed parse can offer a rename hint."*
2. **Same type, same id form, same cardinality.** `reference: z.string().optional()` upstream, `DesignerFieldDefinition.referenceTo?: string` here. Every other site in this repo that names `referenceTo` (`reports.zod.ts`, `filter-builder.tsx`, `designer.ts`) holds a single object machine name too — no array form, no `{object, field}` form anywhere.
3. **The stored values came from the same property.** The `referenceTo` this reads is what `fromDesignerField`'s pre-objectui#6041 emit line wrote, out of the same `designed.referenceTo` that today's `reference: designed.referenceTo` reads.

⇒ **P1 holds.** And it is exactly what separates this from objectui#6043: the alias map lists `formula → expression` too, but those two sides carry **different value grammars** (`expression` is CEL; the retired textarea accepted arbitrary text), so that rename would have laundered non-CEL text into a formula that parses green. There is no value grammar to violate here.

## ⚠️⚠️ An existing pin was flipped — stated in full, never silently

**The case:** `MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx`, the last `describe` in the file — `objectui#7714 · a lookup whose target survives only as 'referenceTo'` › `it('is refused by name, and issues no PUT')`.

**What it pinned:** a stored `{ stale_id: { type: 'lookup', label: 'Stale', referenceTo: 'contact' } }`, an author relabelling an unrelated field, and two assertions — that the page's error surface named `` `stale_id` ``, and that `puts` stayed `[]`.

**What it pins now:** the same document and the same edit, and that the target **survives**: the designer model receives `referenceTo === 'contact'`, the PUT happens, the wire carries `reference: 'contact'` with no `referenceTo` key, and `FieldSchema` parses the emitted field.

**Why the flip is right.** That pin recorded the CONSEQUENCE of the read-side gap, not a contract anyone chose. objectui#7714 said so itself when it wrote the case — *"After objectui#7714 the failure is at least loud and field-named instead of a silent dropped relationship. That is strictly better and it is not a fix: the author still has to re-pick a target the document already held."* — and objectui#8058 was filed at that moment for exactly this. Once the read door finds the target, the guard has nothing to refuse, so the old expectation cannot survive the repair; it is replaced rather than respelled, because the branch it pinned is the branch this card removes.

**Order of measurement, as required:**

| step | reading |
|---|---|
| before the fix | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 13 passed (13)` — the pin is green, pinning the refusal |
| after the fix, pin unedited | `Tests 1 failed \| 13 passed (14)` — the single failure is that case: `TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="metadata-fields-page-error"]`, i.e. the save now succeeds |
| after flipping it | `Tests 15 passed (15)` |

So the pin demonstrably sees this change; it was not edited on a hunch.

## ⛔ objectui#7714's guard is untouched, and the acceptance criterion is two-sided

Not one line of `assertRelationshipTargetPresent`, `describeUnusableTarget` or `RELATIONSHIP_TYPES_REQUIRING_REFERENCE` changed. Both rows are asserted:

| situation | after this change |
|---|---|
| target exists **only** as `referenceTo` | read door finds it ⇒ **no longer** refused, relationship preserved (`objectui#8058 · … › loads with its target, and PUTs it back under the spec spelling`) |
| field really has **no** target under either spelling | **still** refused, **still** by name, still no PUT (`⛔ CONTROL — a lookup with NO target under EITHER spelling is still refused, by name, with no PUT`) |

A third control pins the precedence that keeps the fallback a rename rather than a second contract: `⛔ CONTROL — when both spellings are stored and DISAGREE, the spec spelling wins`. And the pre-existing guard cases are all still green — the half-filled draft, the four unusable-target states plus `null`, and the `master_detail` pair.

⛔ objectui#6041's strip assertion is untouched and green: `a save of an object ALREADY carrying 'referenceTo' puts it back without the key`. The shared fixture still carries **both** keys on `legacy_id`, deliberately — that is what gives the strip something to measure, and it now also pins that `reference` wins.

## The docblock that was false

The `carryOver` tombstone docblock asserted, as settled:

> Two of the four cost nothing: `fromDesignerField` re-emits the lookup target under the spec spelling `reference` on the very next line …

That was true only when the READ found a target, which for this shape it did not. It is rewritten to say what it is conditional on — the read door reading both spellings — and to record that this PR is what made it true, so the next reader cannot restate the conclusion without the premise. It also now names the one path where it is **still** false (below).

## 验收备注 — out of scope, filed, not fixed here

- **Filed as #8896** — the same strip still costs the relationship on the paths with **no read door**. Measured on this branch: a stored `{ parent_id: { type: 'master_detail', label: 'Parent', referenceTo: 'invoice' } }` goes to `partitionStoredFields`' preserved half, is re-emitted as `carryOver(keep.raw)` with no `toDesignerField` in the path, and is refused — `puts=[]`, error `` `parent_id` … and this one has none ``. Worse there than here: a preserved field is read-only on this page, so "Pick the target object" names a control the author cannot reach. metadata-admin's `readFields` (`object-fields-io.ts`) states the same invariant and is the second candidate site. The card also names the registry sentence *"The strip loses nothing"* as the claim to fix at the source, which is a decision about the tombstone contract rather than a local patch.
- **Filed as #8897** — the installed spec pin is **17.4.0**, not the 17.3.0 that three version-qualified measurements in this file, its sibling `MetadataService.ts` and this test file all name. Measured: `reference: '   '` is now refused upstream (`custom` at `reference`), so the docblock's *"Until the pin reaches the fix, this guard is still the only thing refusing `'   '` here"* and the user-visible refusal text *"`@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0 ACCEPTS this value"* are both false against the installed artifact. ⛔ Not a behaviour bug — the guard is right to keep refusing (objectui#8621 ruled that) — but the refusal message is pinned verbatim by both writers' tests, so correcting it flips existing pins and is not a drive-by edit.
- **noted, not filed** — the population question the card raises ("how many stored documents still carry `referenceTo`") is a deployed-tenant data question this repo cannot answer. No time was spent guessing and the deliverable was not reduced for it; the card's own conclusion covers both outcomes.
- **Cross-file line-address citations (objectui#8875 axis).** `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` run at the branch point (`b686ebf7d`) and again at the final commit (`3a200e94a`): population identical (1267), and exactly **two** rows move — `plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.referenceArms-6837.test.tsx:49` and `plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.referenceArms-6837.test.tsx:50`, both citing `MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx:75`. At the branch point that line was **blank** (`[non-substantive] (cited line reads '')`) while the citation claims it names a `referenceTo` fixture — so both were **class (B): already not pointing at their subject on `origin/main`**, not addresses this PR knocked off target. ⛔ Untouched; they belong to objectui#8875.

## Verification

Run at the final commit `3a200e94a`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 15 passed (15)`
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/` → `Test Files 18 passed (18) · Tests 142 passed (142)`
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/plugin-designer^...' run build` → 15 of 47 projects, all `Done` (the dependency closure; without it `type-check` answers `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'`, which is PREREQUISITE NOT MET, not a red gate)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-designer run type-check` → exit 0. ⚠️ That project **excludes** `*.test.tsx` (`--listFiles` count for the changed test file: 0), so the test file is covered by `tsconfig.test.json` instead: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit --listFiles` → exit 0, changed test file present in the program (count 1), zero `error TS`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` → `✅ 2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`
- `pnpm run check:designer-field-key-parity` → `designer-field-key-parity: OK`
- `pnpm run check:control-bytes` → `✅ OK (scanned 7086 tracked text file(s))`, plus a direct `grep -naP` over the three changed paths: no match
- `pnpm run check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `check:vi-mock-inherit` / `check:spec-symbols` → all `✅ OK`
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the three changed paths → `✅ NOT GOVERNED`
- **Lint, and why this is a measurement rather than a skipped run.** `pnpm lint` here is `turbo run lint` — per-package `eslint .` — and the diff touches one package, so the affected unit is run whole: `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` inside `packages/plugin-designer` → exit 0, **53 files** linted (count read from the JSON output), 0 errors, 66 pre-existing warnings, none of them in either changed file. Invariance for the packages not run: `eslint.config.js` configures no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so no rule here is type-aware and no verdict on an untouched file can move with this diff.

## Clause-②

`Clause-②: yes` — judged by this seat and appended to the claim comment on #8058 under the dispatch's carrier pre-authorization. No new exported symbol and no new key on a published payload, but the read door now honours a second spelling, so a stored document that previously produced a target-less `lookup` now produces one carrying `reference`. That is an acceptance-set widening on the surface AGENTS.md #0.1 governs, and the card had to argue against objectui#6043 to reach it. This PR parks in draft awaiting the contract-review tier; `needs:contract-review` is attached.
